title.en: Common division and the HCF–LCM product check

text.en: Two classes have 18 and 24 students. They need the largest team size that works with both class sizes. Zara sets up a common-division table.

Divide both numbers by a prime that divides them exactly. Continue until the remaining numbers have no common divisor greater than one. The product of primes used is the HCF. For two positive integers, HCF × LCM equals their product.
Use a prime divisor that works for both numbers. Divide both by three to get six and eight.
Divide both by two. This leaves three and four.
Three and four have no common prime divisor. Multiply the common prime divisors that we used.
Check the relationship by finding the least common multiple, seventy-two. Six times seventy-two equals the product of eighteen and twenty-four.

problem.en: Use common division to find the HCF and LCM of 20 and 30.

text.en: Divide both by 2, then both by 5.

why.en: The remaining 2 and 3 have no common factor greater than 1.
For two positive integers, HCF × LCM equals the product of the integers.

prompt.en: When do you stop common division, and what do you multiply?

requiredIdeas.en: Stop when the remaining numbers share no prime divisor.
Multiply the common primes used in order.

points.en: Only common divisors belong in an HCF division table.
For two positive integers, use the product to check HCF and LCM.
